This is a list of some of the more commonly known problems that are [[NP-complete]] when expressed as [[decision problem]]s. As there are thousands of such problems known, this list is in no way comprehensive. Many problems of this type can be found in {{harvtxt|Garey|Johnson|1979}}.

==Graphs and hypergraphs==
[[Graph theory|Graphs]] occur frequently in everyday applications. Examples include biological or social networks, which contain hundreds, thousands and even billions of nodes in some cases (e.g. [[Facebook]] or [[LinkedIn]]). 
*[[1-planar graph|1-planarity]]{{sfnp|Grigoriev|Bodlaender|2007}}
*[[3-dimensional matching]]<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979">{{harvtxt|Garey|Johnson|1979}}</ref>{{rp|SP1}}
*[[Bandwidth problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT40}}
*[[Bipartite dimension]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT18}}
*[[Capacitated minimum spanning tree]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND5}}
*[[Route inspection problem]] (also called '''Chinese postman problem''') for [[mixed graph]]s (having both directed and undirected edges). The program is solvable in polynomial time if the graph has all undirected or all directed edges. Variants include the rural postman problem.<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND25, ND27}}
*[[Clique cover problem]]<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT17}}
*[[Clique problem]]<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT19}}
*[[Complete coloring]], a.k.a. achromatic number<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT5}}
*[[Cycle rank]] 
*[[Degree-constrained spanning tree]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND1}}
*[[Domatic number]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT3}}
*[[Dominating set problem|Dominating set]], a.k.a. domination number<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT2}}
::NP-complete special cases include the [[edge dominating set]] problem, i.e., the dominating set problem in line graphs. NP-complete variants include the [[connected dominating set]] problem and the [[maximum leaf spanning tree]] problem.<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND2}}
*[[Feedback vertex set]]<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT7}}
*[[Feedback arc set]]<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT8}}
*[[Graph coloring]]<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT4}}
*[[Graph homomorphism]] problem<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT52}}
*[[Graph partition]] into [[Glossary of graph theory#Subgraphs|subgraphs]] of specific types (triangles, [[graph isomorphism|isomorphic]] [[Glossary of graph theory#Subgraphs|subgraphs]], [[Hamiltonian graph|Hamiltonian]] subgraphs, [[forest (graph theory)|forests]], [[perfect matching]]s) are known NP-complete. Partition into [[Glossary of graph theory#Cliques|cliques]] is the same problem as [[graph coloring|coloring]] the [[Complement (graph theory)|complement]] of the given graph. A related problem is to find a partition that is optimal terms of the number of edges between parts.<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT11, GT12, GT13, GT14, GT15, GT16, ND14}}
*[[Grundy number]] of a directed graph.<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT56}}
*[[Hamiltonian completion]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT34}}
*[[Hamiltonian path problem]], directed and undirected.<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT37, GT38, GT39}}
*[[Induced subgraph isomorphism problem]]
*[[Intersection number (graph theory)|Graph intersection number]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT59}}
*[[Longest path problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND29}}
*Maximum bipartite subgraph or (especially with weighted edges) [[maximum cut]].<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT25, ND16}}
*[[Maximum common subgraph isomorphism problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT49}}
*[[Maximum independent set]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT20}}
*Maximum [[Induced path]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT23}}
*[[Minimum maximal independent set]] a.k.a. minimum independent dominating set<ref>[http://www.csc.kth.se/~viggo/wwwcompendium/node14.html Minimum Independent Dominating Set]</ref>
::NP-complete special cases include the [[minimum maximal matching]] problem,<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT10}} which is essentially equal to the [[edge dominating set]] problem (see above).
*[[Metric dimension (graph theory)|Metric dimension]] of a graph<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT61}}
*[[Metric k-center]]
*[[Minimum degree spanning tree]]
*[[Minimum k-cut]]
*[[Minimum k-spanning tree]]
*[[Minor (graph theory)|Minor]] testing (checking whether an input graph <math>G</math> contains an input graph <math>H</math> as a minor); the same holds with topological minors
*[[Steiner tree problem|Steiner tree]], or [[Minimum spanning tree]] for a subset of the vertices of a graph.<ref name="karp"/> (The minimum spanning tree for an entire graph is solvable in polynomial time.)
*[[Modularity (networks)|Modularity maximization]]<ref>{{citation | title = Maximizing Modularity is hard | first1 = Ulrik | last1 = Brandes | author1-link = Ulrik Brandes | first2 = Daniel | last2 = Delling | first3 = Marco | last3 = Gaertler | first4 = Robert | last4 = Görke | first5 = Martin | last5 = Hoefer | first6 = Zoran | last6 = Nikoloski | first7 = Dorothea | last7 = Wagner | year = 2006 | arxiv = physics/0608255| bibcode = 2006physics...8255B }}</ref>
*[[Monochromatic triangle]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT6}}
*[[Pathwidth]],<ref name="acp1987"/> or, equivalently, [[Path decomposition#Interval thickness|interval thickness]], and [[Path decomposition#Vertex separation number|vertex separation number]]<ref>{{harvtxt|Kashiwabara|Fujisawa|1979}}; {{harvtxt|Ohtsuki|Mori|Kuh|Kashiwabara|1979}}; {{harvtxt|Lengauer|1981}}.</ref>
*Rank coloring
*[[Route inspection problem#Variants|k-Chinese postman]]
*[[Shortest total path length spanning tree]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND3}}
*[[Slope number]] two testing<ref name=Comp2Planar>{{cite book|title=Lecture Notes in Computer Science| year=1995| volume=894/1995 | pages=286–297| doi=10.1007/3-540-58950-3_384 | chapter=On the computational complexity of upward and rectilinear planarity testing| last1=Garg| first1=Ashim| last2=Tamassia| first2=Roberto| isbn=978-3-540-58950-1}}</ref>
*Recognizing [[string graph]]s<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schaefer |first1=Marcus |last2=Sedgwick |first2=Eric |last3=Štefankovič |first3=Daniel |title=Recognizing string graphs in NP |journal=Journal of Computer and System Sciences |date=September 2003 |volume=67 |issue=2 |pages=365–380 |doi=10.1016/S0022-0000(03)00045-X|doi-access=free }}</ref>
*[[Subgraph isomorphism problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT48}}
*[[Treewidth]]<ref name="acp1987">{{harvtxt|Arnborg|Corneil|Proskurowski|1987}}</ref>
*Testing whether a [[tree (graph theory)|tree]] may be represented as [[Euclidean minimum spanning tree]]
*[[Vertex cover]]<ref name="karp">{{harvtxt|Karp|1972}}</ref><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|GT1}}
*Minimum [[Wiener connector]] problem

==Mathematical programming==
*[[3-partition problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|SP15}}
*[[Bin packing problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|SR1}}
*[[Bottleneck traveling salesman]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND24}}
*[[Optimal facility location#Uncapacited facility location|Uncapacitated facility location problem]]
*[[Flow Shop Scheduling Problem]]
*[[Generalized assignment problem]]
*[[Integer programming]]. The variant where variables are required to be 0 or 1, called zero-one linear programming, and several other variants are also NP-complete<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|MP1}}
*Some problems related to [[job-shop scheduling]]
*[[Knapsack problem]], [[quadratic knapsack problem]], and several variants<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|MP9}}
*Some problems related to [[multiprocessor scheduling]]
*[[Numerical 3-dimensional matching]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|SP16}}
*[[Open-shop scheduling]]
*[[Partition problem]]<ref name="karp"/><ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|SP12}}
*[[Quadratic assignment problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND43}}
*[[Quadratic programming]] (NP-hard in some cases, P if convex)
*[[Subset sum problem]]<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|SP13}}
*Variations on the [[traveling salesman problem]]. The problem for graphs is NP-complete if the edge lengths are assumed integers. The problem for points on the plane is NP-complete with the discretized Euclidean metric and rectilinear metric. The problem is known to be NP-hard with the (non-discretized) Euclidean metric.<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND22, ND23}}

*By the same article<ref name="NP-complete decision problems for Quadratic Polynomials" /> existence of bounded [[Tonelli–Shanks algorithm|modular square roots]] with arbitrarily composite modulus. Given positive integers <math>\textstyle A,B,C \geq 0</math>, decide existence of an integer <math>x\in[0,C]</math> such that <math>x^2\equiv A\bmod B</math>. The problem remains NP-complete even if a [[Prime number#Unique factorization|prime factorization]] of <math>B</math> is provided.

I-SPAN'02 |chapter=Block sorting is hard |date=2002-01-01|pages=307–312|doi=10.1109/ISPAN.2002.1004305|isbn=978-0-7695-1579-3|s2cid=32222403}}</ref> (Sorting by Block Moves)
*[[Sparse approximation]]
*Variations of the [[Steiner tree problem]]. Specifically, with the discretized Euclidean metric, rectilinear metric. The problem is known to be NP-hard with the (non-discretized) Euclidean metric.<ref name="gj1979" />{{rp|ND13}}
*Three-dimensional [[Ising model]]<ref>[[Barry Arthur Cipra]], "The Ising Model Is NP-Complete", SIAM News, Vol 33, No 6.</ref>
<!--
Propositional logic problems, in particular satisfiability problems and their variants, are of particular practical interest because many practical problems can be solved by expressing them as satisfiability problems, and then using efficient [[SAT solver]]s to obtain an exact solution quickly{{Citation needed|date=November 2010}}.
-->
